unibuc.about: One of the oldest state universities in the country, with 20 faculties of science, law, letters and social sciences. It is known for its tradition and its wide range of programmes.
unibuc.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
unibuc.admission: The admission method differs from one faculty to another: at some the Romanian Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, at others an exam or a written test. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
unibuc.scholarshipsNote: You can receive merit scholarships for good grades, and social scholarships if your family's situation requires it.
unibuc.dormsNote: It has student dormitories, but places are limited and are usually given according to grades.
pros: A great many programmes, so it is easier to change direction
A name known in the country and abroad, useful on a CV
Based in the centre of the capital, with a rich cultural life
cons: The city is expensive, especially the rent
The faculties are crowded, with large groups
Few dormitory places compared with the number of students

upb.about: The largest engineering school in the country, with engineering and computer science faculties in Bucharest, plus the Pitești University Centre (the former University of Pitești, with which it merged), which also has faculties of science, economics, law and letters. It is known for graduates that companies look for.
upb.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
upb.admission: At most faculties you get in on the basis of your file, with your high-school grades in subjects such as mathematics and physics; for Automatic Control and Computers and for part of Electronics you take a written exam. The rules differ by faculty, so check the admission regulations.
upb.scholarshipsNote: There are merit and social scholarships, and some students can also receive performance scholarships.
upb.dormsNote: There are student dormitories; there are few compared with the demand, so apply early.
pros: Its students are in great demand with IT and engineering firms
Many technical faculties in one place
A large campus with dormitories and student activities
cons: The courses are hard and many students fall behind
The big faculties have crowded groups
The campus in the capital is far from the centre

ase-bucuresti.about: The best-known university of economics in the country, with faculties of finance, management, marketing and economic informatics. It is recognised by employers in the financial field.
ase-bucuresti.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
ase-bucuresti.admission: The admission method differs from one faculty to another: at some the Romanian Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, at others an exam or a written test. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
ase-bucuresti.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
ase-bucuresti.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: A degree valued in banks, companies and consulting
Many business and finance programmes
Partnerships with companies for placements and internships
cons: Strong competition for the most sought-after faculties
Many students each year, so large groups
Bucharest rents raise the costs

umf-carol-davila.about: The oldest and largest medical university in the country, with faculties of medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, and midwifery and nursing. Check the university's website to see in which Bucharest hospitals the practical training takes place.
umf-carol-davila.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
umf-carol-davila.admission: For medicine and dentistry you take a multiple-choice test in biology and, as you choose, chemistry or physics; for pharmacy, in organic chemistry and biology. For midwifery and nursing you get in with your file, based on your Baccalaureate (bac) average and your high-school average. A medical certificate is also required.
umf-carol-davila.scholarshipsNote: You can receive merit scholarships for good grades, and social scholarships if your family's situation requires it.
umf-carol-davila.dormsNote: It has student dormitories, but places are limited and are usually given according to grades.
pros: Practical training in large, varied hospitals in the capital
A degree recognised in Europe
Many medical programmes in the same place
cons: Very competitive admission
The schedule is heavy and demands a lot of study
Rent and living costs in Bucharest are high

snspa.about: A state school focused on political science, administration, communication and public management. It suits you if you want a career in institutions, diplomacy or communication.
snspa.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
snspa.admission: The admission method differs from one faculty to another: at some the Romanian Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, at others an exam or a written test. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
snspa.scholarshipsNote: There are merit and social scholarships, and some students can also receive performance scholarships.
snspa.dormsNote: There are student dormitories; there are few compared with the demand, so apply early.
pros: Clear specialisation in administration and politics
Smaller groups than at the big universities
Links with public institutions and organisations
cons: It does not offer a great variety of fields
You may end up with a narrow degree if you change your mind
Few state-funded places

uauim.about: The main school of architecture in Bucharest, named after the architect Ion Mincu. It trains architects, urban planners and landscape specialists.
uauim.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
uauim.admission: For architecture you take a single practical drawing test (graphic representation), held at the university's premises, which counts the most; the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts too. No portfolio is required, and the exercises differ by programme. For Urbanism and Territorial Administration (Sibiu) you get in with an eliminatory online interview and the Baccalaureate (bac) average.
uauim.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
uauim.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: The only faculty in the capital dedicated solely to architecture
Practical studio work and projects from the first year
A degree valued in the country and in Europe
cons: The programme is long and demanding (6 years)
A lot of time spent on projects, sometimes at night
Materials for models cost money

utcb.about: A technical state university for construction, with faculties of civil engineering, hydrotechnics, geodesy and building services. It trains engineers for building sites and design.
utcb.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
utcb.admission: You get in without an exam, with your Baccalaureate (bac) results: for engineering, the bac average counts together with the mathematics grade. For programmes in foreign languages you also take a language test, graded pass or fail. Check the admission regulations.
utcb.scholarshipsNote: You can receive merit scholarships for good grades, and social scholarships if your family's situation requires it.
utcb.dormsNote: It has student dormitories, but places are limited and are usually given according to grades.
pros: Construction always has a demand for engineers
Clear, practical programmes
Close links with construction companies
cons: Fewer fields than at a large university
Mathematics and physics are hard
Work on building sites can be demanding

usamv-bucuresti.about: A state university for agriculture, horticulture, veterinary medicine and animal science. It has its own farms and laboratories for practical training.
usamv-bucuresti.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
usamv-bucuresti.admission: At almost all faculties you get in without an exam: the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts the most, plus the grade in a bac exam of your choice. For veterinary medicine in Romanian you take a written test in biology and chemistry, which counts the most. Check the regulations.
usamv-bucuresti.scholarshipsNote: There are merit and social scholarships, and some students can also receive performance scholarships.
usamv-bucuresti.dormsNote: There are student dormitories; there are few compared with the demand, so apply early.
pros: Practical training on its own farm and in its own laboratories
A field with a real need for specialists
A green campus in Bucharest
cons: It may involve work outside the city
Fewer faculties than other universities
Prestige is lower outside its field

unatc.about: The most important theatre and film school in the country, named after I.L. Caragiale. It trains actors, directors, cinematographers and screenwriters.
unatc.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
unatc.admission: Admission is through talent tests and an interview, not just grades; you are asked to show what you can do. Details differ by programme.
unatc.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
unatc.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: Teachers who are well-known actors and directors
A lot of practical work, on stage or in front of the camera
You can work on films and shows while still at university
cons: Very hard admission, with few places
The profession has an uncertain income
The schedule is intense and irregular

unmb.about: A state university for music, with programmes in performance, composition and musicology. Students play in concerts and auditions.
unmb.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
unmb.admission: Admission is only through music tests: a recital on an instrument or in voice, and tests in theory, solfège and dictation; the Baccalaureate (bac) only has to be passed. You are asked to show what you can do. Details differ by programme.
unmb.scholarshipsNote: You can receive merit scholarships for good grades, and social scholarships if your family's situation requires it.
unmb.dormsNote: It has student dormitories, but places are limited and are usually given according to grades.
pros: Individual lessons with teachers who are musicians
Many concerts and chances to perform in public
Its own dormitory and music library
cons: It requires years of musical study before admission
The job market for musicians is small
A lot of daily practice time

unarte.about: A state university for fine arts, design and decorative arts, with studios for painting, graphic art, sculpture and design. It trains artists and designers.
unarte.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
unarte.admission: You get in on the basis of practical drawing or specialist tests, the first of which is eliminatory, followed by an interview in which you present your portfolio of works. The Baccalaureate (bac) average only counts as a tie-breaker. Details differ by programme.
unarte.scholarshipsNote: There are merit and social scholarships, and some students can also receive performance scholarships.
unarte.dormsNote: There are student dormitories; there are few compared with the demand, so apply early.
pros: Studios with plenty of space and materials for practice
Varied creative fields: painting, design, fashion
Exhibitions and projects from your time at university
cons: Admission with drawing tests and strong competition
Uncertain income at the start of a career
Art materials can cost money

unefs.about: A state university for physical education and sport, with programmes for coach, sports teacher and physiotherapy. It has its own gyms and sports facilities.
unefs.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
unefs.admission: Besides the Baccalaureate (bac) average, you have to pass physical or sports tests and you need a medical certificate. Details differ by programme.
unefs.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
unefs.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: Its own sports facilities for training
Training for active careers: coach, physiotherapist
Classmates who are passionate about movement
cons: Good physical condition is required at admission
A narrow specialisation, in sport and movement
Jobs can be seasonal

academia-politie.about: A state institution of the Ministry of Internal Affairs that trains police officers, border police, gendarmes and firefighters, with studies in law, public order and safety, and building services. Graduates have a job guaranteed at the end of their studies.
academia-politie.budgetNote: For full-time courses the places are state-funded, and the academy also pays for accommodation, meals and equipment. Only the distance-learning Law programme is fee-paying.
academia-politie.admission: Admission requires written tests, physical tests and a medical check, as at any military institution; strict entry rules apply. Ask the institution for information.
academia-politie.scholarshipsNote: On full-time courses you receive accommodation, food, equipment and medical care free of charge during your studies. Check with the academy whether you also receive money monthly.
academia-politie.dormsNote: Accommodation and meals are provided on site, usually for the whole period of study.
pros: You have a secure job after graduation
You receive accommodation and food during your studies
Law training and practice in the field
cons: Strict discipline and a demanding schedule
After graduation you work for a number of years in the system
The physical and medical tests eliminate many candidates

atm.about: A state military institution that trains officer-engineers in fields such as electronics, mechanics, computer science and military construction. Students also receive military training.
atm.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
atm.admission: For the state-funded places you first pass the selection made by the institution recruiting you (medical, sports and psychological tests), then take a multiple-choice test in mathematics, computer science and physics. For fee-paying places you get in on the Baccalaureate (bac) average. Ask the institution for information.
atm.scholarshipsNote: You receive accommodation, food and a monthly allowance during your studies, on top of the usual scholarships.
atm.dormsNote: On state-funded places, accommodation in the dormitory on site and meals are provided free of charge during your studies. Students on fee-paying places do not receive accommodation and meals.
pros: Technical studies plus military training
Accommodation, food and an allowance provided
A guaranteed post in the army after graduation
cons: Barracks life is strict, with a fixed schedule
You are obliged to work in the army for a number of years
Admission with physical and medical tests

ubb-cluj.about: The largest university in the country, teaching in Romanian, Hungarian and German, across more than 20 faculties. It is known for research and for its wide range of programmes.
ubb-cluj.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
ubb-cluj.admission: The admission method differs from one faculty to another: at some the Romanian Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, at others an exam or a written test. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
ubb-cluj.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
ubb-cluj.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: The most varied range of faculties in the country
Teaching also in Hungarian or German, on some programmes
A young city, full of student events
cons: Cluj-Napoca is an expensive city
Strong competition for the popular faculties
Not enough dormitory places for the number of students

utcn.about: A technical state university, with faculties of automatic control, electronics, construction, mechanics and architecture. It is one of the best engineering schools in the country.
utcn.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
utcn.admission: At most faculties you get in through a competition of files, with your Baccalaureate (bac) average and grades. For Automatic Control and Computers there is a multiple-choice test in mathematics, and for Architecture a drawing test; the rules differ by faculty, so check the admission guide.
utcn.scholarshipsNote: You can receive merit scholarships for good grades, and social scholarships if your family's situation requires it.
utcn.dormsNote: It has student dormitories in two complexes in Cluj-Napoca and in Baia Mare; places are limited and are requested by application at the start of the academic year.
pros: Highly valued by IT companies in Cluj
Good teachers and laboratories for computers
Many students do placements in companies while still at university
cons: The courses are hard and demand a lot of work
Rents in Cluj are high
Competitive admission for computers

umf-cluj.about: A university of medicine and pharmacy in Cluj, with programmes also in Romanian, English and French. It is among the most respected medical schools in the country.
umf-cluj.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
umf-cluj.admission: For medicine and dental medicine there is a multiple-choice written exam in biology and organic chemistry, and for pharmacy in biology or organic chemistry. For shorter programmes, such as nursing, your high-school and Baccalaureate (bac) averages count. A medical certificate is also required.
umf-cluj.scholarshipsNote: There are performance scholarships, for good academic results, and social scholarships; students with outstanding scientific results can also receive a scientific scholarship.
umf-cluj.dormsNote: There are student dormitories; there are few compared with the demand, so apply early.
pros: Large clinical hospitals in the same city
Teaching also in English or French on some programmes
Graduates valued in the country and abroad
cons: Hard admission, with a lot of competition
The schedule is heavy
Living in Cluj is expensive

usamv-cluj.about: A state university for agriculture, horticulture, veterinary medicine and food technology. It has teaching farms and a campus with green spaces.
usamv-cluj.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
usamv-cluj.admission: At almost all faculties you get in with the Baccalaureate (bac) average. For veterinary medicine, besides the bac average, you also take two short multiple-choice tests, in biology and chemistry. Check the guide.
usamv-cluj.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
usamv-cluj.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: Practical training on its own farms and in its own laboratories
Fields in demand in agriculture and the food industry
A large city with many work opportunities
cons: Fewer fields than the big universities
Practical work can mean hours in the field or on the farm
Rent in Cluj is expensive

uad-cluj.about: A state university for fine arts, design and decorative arts, with studios for painting, sculpture, graphic art and design. It is one of the well-known art schools in the country.
uad-cluj.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
uad-cluj.admission: You get in on the basis of a practical specialist test and an interview based on your portfolio of works, which count equally. The Baccalaureate (bac) only counts as a tie-breaker, when averages are equal. For art history and theory, a motivation letter is assessed, and the bac average makes up half of the final grade.
uad-cluj.scholarshipsNote: You can receive performance scholarships for good results, and social scholarships if your family's situation requires it.
uad-cluj.dormsNote: It has two student dormitories; places are limited and are requested by application, by the deadlines announced by the university. Most places are given by grade average, and some are kept for social cases.
pros: Well-equipped studios for creative work
Varied fields: design, photography, graphic art, ceramics
An active art scene in Cluj
cons: Admission with practical tests and strong competition
Uncertain income after graduation
Materials for projects can cost money

amgd-cluj.about: A state academy for music, with programmes in performance, composition and music pedagogy. It is named after the composer Gheorghe Dima.
amgd-cluj.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
amgd-cluj.admission: Admission is through specialist tests, for example performance on an instrument or in voice, or solfège and a music theory test, not just grades; you are asked to show what you can do. Details differ by programme.
amgd-cluj.scholarshipsNote: There are study scholarships and merit scholarships, based on grade average, and social scholarships.
amgd-cluj.dormsNote: There are student dormitories; there are few compared with the demand, so apply early.
pros: Individual lessons with specialist teachers
Concerts and projects in the cultural city of Transylvania
A dormitory dedicated to students
cons: It requires serious musical training beforehand
The job market is small for musicians
A lot of individual daily practice

uaic.about: The oldest university in the country, founded in 1860, with faculties of science, law, letters, economics and many more. It is an important university centre in Moldavia.
uaic.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
uaic.admission: The admission method differs from one faculty to another: at some the Romanian Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, at others an exam or a written test. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
uaic.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
uaic.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: It has great tradition and prestige, since 1860
A wide range of programmes in a single city
Iași is cheaper than the capital and Cluj
cons: The sought-after faculties are crowded
The city is far from the west and from the capital
Few dormitory places compared with demand

tuiasi.about: A technical state university, with faculties of automatic control, electronics, construction, mechanics, chemistry and architecture. It is the largest technical university in the region and among the top in the country, with a tradition of over two centuries in training engineers.
tuiasi.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
tuiasi.admission: At most faculties you get in through a competition of files, with your Baccalaureate (bac) average or grades. For Automatic Control and Computers there is a multiple-choice test in mathematics or computer science, and for Architecture a drawing test; check the rules of your faculty.
tuiasi.scholarshipsNote: You can receive merit scholarships for good grades, and social scholarships if your family's situation requires it.
tuiasi.dormsNote: It has student dormitories, but places are limited and are usually given according to grades.
pros: A varied technical offer, from IT to construction
Living costs lower than in Cluj or Bucharest
IT companies in Iași hire many graduates
cons: Mathematics and physics demand a lot of effort
Some buildings and laboratories are older
Competition for state-funded places in computers

umf-iasi.about: A university of medicine in Iași, with medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and nursing. It is one of the largest medical schools in the country.
umf-iasi.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
umf-iasi.admission: Admission is through a competition with a written, multiple-choice test for bachelor's programmes; the exam subjects differ by programme, so check the methodology. A medical certificate is also required.
umf-iasi.scholarshipsNote: There are merit and social scholarships, and some students can also receive performance scholarships.
umf-iasi.dormsNote: There are student dormitories; there are few compared with the demand, so apply early.
pros: Large university hospitals in Iași
Living costs lower than in other big cities
Programmes in Romanian and in English
cons: Competitive admission
The schedule is heavy
There can be many students in a course

iuls.about: A state university for agriculture, horticulture, animal science and veterinary medicine, with practice farms. It is named after the agronomist Ion Ionescu de la Brad.
iuls.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
iuls.admission: You get in without an exam, through a competition based on your Baccalaureate (bac) grades: the grade from the written Romanian language test and the grade from another written test of your choice. The same rule applies to veterinary medicine. Check the methodology.
iuls.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
iuls.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: Its own farms and stations for practice
Fields in demand in agriculture and food
Iași offers cheaper living than other big cities
cons: Fewer fields than at a large university
Practical work can be outside the city
Prestige is lower outside its field

arte-iasi.about: A state university for the arts, with programmes in music, fine arts, design and theatre. It is named after the composer George Enescu.
arte-iasi.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
arte-iasi.admission: Admission is through talent tests and an interview, not just grades; you are asked to show what you can do. Details differ by programme.
arte-iasi.scholarshipsNote: You can receive merit scholarships for good grades, and social scholarships if your family's situation requires it.
arte-iasi.dormsNote: It has one student dormitory in Iași; places are limited and are requested at the start of the academic year, from the accommodation committee.
pros: Brings together music, visual arts and theatre
Small groups and attention from teachers
A rich cultural life in Iași
cons: Admission with talent tests, with few places
Uncertain income in the arts
Facilities differ from one field to another

uvt.about: A state university in Timișoara, with faculties of science, letters, economics, law, arts and others. It is a university centre open to Western Europe.
uvt.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
uvt.admission: For each programme you take an admission test: a test of knowledge in the field, the UVT test of language and reasoning skills or, in arts, music and sport, aptitude tests. At some faculties the Baccalaureate (bac) grades also count. Read the regulations of the faculty you are interested in.
uvt.scholarshipsNote: There are performance scholarships and social scholarships, and some students can also receive special scholarships or scholarships for sporting performance.
uvt.dormsNote: There are student dormitories; there are few compared with the demand, so apply early.
pros: A varied offer, from computer science to the arts
A multicultural city, close to the border with Western Europe
Many foreign students, so an international environment
cons: Competition for state-funded places at some faculties
Dormitories with limited places
Rent in Timișoara has gone up

upt.about: A technical state university in Timișoara, with faculties of automatic control, electronics, mechanics, construction, chemistry and architecture. It is known for its links with industry in the west.
upt.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
upt.admission: At most faculties you get in through a competition of files, with the Baccalaureate (bac) average. For Automatic Control and Computers you take a test in mathematics or computer science or present a portfolio, and for Architecture a practical test and an interview; check the admission guide.
upt.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
upt.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: Large companies in Timișoara hire graduates
Modern laboratories at some faculties
A dynamic, young city
cons: The courses are difficult
Rent in Timișoara is rising
Crowding at the popular faculties

umft.about: A university of medicine in Timișoara, with medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and nursing. It also offers programmes in English and French.
umft.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
umft.admission: For medicine and dental medicine there is a multiple-choice test in biology and chemistry. For pharmacy and the other programmes there is a multiple-choice test in biology, and the Baccalaureate (bac) also counts towards the average. A medical certificate is also required.
umft.scholarshipsNote: You can receive merit scholarships for good grades, and social scholarships if your family's situation requires it.
umft.dormsNote: It has student dormitories, but places are limited; the accommodation request (pre-accommodation) is made online, in good time. Students in later years have priority, and the grade average counts mainly for the dormitories with two-person rooms.
pros: Programmes in Romanian, English and French
University hospitals in the city
International students, so a mixed environment
cons: Very competitive admission
The schedule is demanding
Living in Timișoara costs more

usvt.about: A state university for agriculture, horticulture, veterinary medicine and rural tourism, in Timișoara. It has its own farms and research stations.
usvt.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
usvt.admission: You get in on the basis of your file, without an exam: the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts most, along with the average of your high-school years. Check the admission guide of your faculty.
usvt.scholarshipsNote: The university gives performance scholarships, for good academic results, and social scholarships; there are also special scholarships and scholarships for sporting performance. You can find the conditions in the scholarship regulations.
usvt.dormsNote: There are dormitories on campus, but places are limited: first-year students have priority, and the others are chosen by grade average. Students from Timișoara and nearby do not get a place.
pros: Its own farms and laboratories for practice
Also includes newer fields such as rural tourism
A city with a developed job market
cons: Fewer fields than at a large university
Practical work can be outside the city
Lower prestige outside its field

unitbv.about: A large state university in Brașov, with faculties of engineering, forestry, economics, medicine, law and music. It is known for its varied offer and modern campus.
unitbv.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
unitbv.admission: The admission method differs from one faculty to another: at most the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, at Medicine there is a written test, and at Music aptitude tests. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
unitbv.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
unitbv.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.

A mountain city, ideal for winter sports
A campus with dormitories and faculties close together

Winter is long and cold
Few dormitory places compared with the number of requests

ucv.about: A state university in Craiova, with faculties of science, engineering, economics, law and letters. It is the main university centre in the south of Oltenia.
ucv.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
ucv.admission: The admission method differs from one faculty to another: at most the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, at a few there is also a written test, and for sport, music and theatre there are aptitude tests. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
ucv.scholarshipsNote: The university gives performance and merit scholarships, for good academic results, and social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the scholarship regulations.
ucv.dormsNote: It has student dormitories, but places are limited and are usually given according to grades.
pros: A varied offer for the south of the country
Living costs lower than in the big cities
Groups that are sometimes smaller, with more attention
cons: A city with fewer IT job opportunities
Lower prestige than the big universities
Some faculties have old laboratories

umf-craiova.about: A university of medicine in Craiova, with medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and nursing. It is the main medical school in the south of Oltenia.
umf-craiova.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
umf-craiova.admission: For all programmes there is an admission exam: biology and organic chemistry for medicine, dental medicine and pharmacy, and biology only for the others. A medical certificate is also required.
umf-craiova.scholarshipsNote: There are performance scholarships, for good academic results, social scholarships and special scholarships.
umf-craiova.dormsNote: There are student dormitories; there are few compared with the demand, so apply early.
pros: A university hospital in Craiova
Living costs lower than in the big cities
Smaller groups, with more attention
cons: Competitive admission
A heavy schedule
A smaller city, with a limited cultural life

ovidius.about: A state university in Constanța, with faculties of law, letters, medicine, science, economics and others. It has the advantage of a city by the sea.
ovidius.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
ovidius.admission: The admission method differs from one faculty to another: at some the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, at Medicine there is a written exam, and at Arts there are aptitude tests. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
ovidius.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
ovidius.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: You study by the sea, with summer life
Many faculties, including medicine and law
A city with a port and tourism, so job opportunities
cons: In winter the city is quieter
Dormitories with limited places
Lower prestige than universities in the big centres

umc.about: A state university in Constanța that trains merchant navy officers and naval engineers. Students do practical training on ships.
umc.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
umc.admission: You get in on the basis of your file, without an exam: the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts and, for state-funded places, also the mathematics grade from the bac. For programmes in English a language test or certificate is also required.
umc.scholarshipsNote: You can receive performance scholarships for good results, and social scholarships if your family's situation requires it.
umc.dormsNote: It has student dormitories, but places are limited and are usually given according to grades.
pros: Practical training on ships and the possibility of working abroad
A profession with high salaries for seafarers
A clear specialisation, with a global market
cons: Life at sea means months away from home
Good medical condition is required
A very specialised field

anmb.about: A state military institution in Constanța that trains naval officers. It also has a civilian section, with programmes in navigation and naval engineering.
anmb.budgetNote: In the military section the places are state-funded, with no fee. In the civilian section the places are fee-paying, and the best-ranked students can receive a scholarship from the academy.
anmb.admission: In the military section you first go through recruitment and selection, with aptitude tests and a medical examination, then take a multiple-choice test in mathematics, computer science and physics. In the civilian section you get in on the basis of your file, with the Baccalaureate (bac) average.
anmb.scholarshipsNote: Military students receive accommodation, food and equipment free of charge and have a monthly pay (soldă), but they do not receive scholarships. Students in the civilian section can receive study, performance or social scholarships.
anmb.dormsNote: Military students have accommodation provided for the whole period of their studies, and food and equipment are free. Civilian students can get a place in a dormitory, as places allow.
pros: Secure jobs in the Navy
Accommodation and food provided during your studies
Practical training on ships
cons: A strict life, with military discipline
You are obliged to work in the army for a number of years
Admission with physical and medical tests

ulbs.about: A state university in Sibiu, with faculties of engineering, medicine, law, letters, theology and economics. It is known for the atmosphere of the old town.
ulbs.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
ulbs.admission: The admission method differs from one faculty to another: at some the Romanian Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, at others an exam or a written test. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
ulbs.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
ulbs.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: A beautiful, safe city that is easy to get around on foot
A varied offer, including medicine and engineering
Partnerships with companies in the area
cons: A smaller city, with fewer opportunities than Cluj
Competition for state-funded places in medicine
Not enough dormitories

ugal.about: A state university in Galați, with faculties of naval engineering, computer science, law, letters and medicine. It is known for fields linked to the Danube and industry.
ugal.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
ugal.admission: The admission method differs from one faculty to another: at some the Romanian Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, at others an exam or a written test. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
ugal.scholarshipsNote: You can receive merit scholarships for good grades, and social scholarships if your family's situation requires it.
ugal.dormsNote: It has student dormitories, but places are limited and are usually given according to grades.
pros: Specialisation in naval and industrial engineering
Low living costs
A city on the Danube with a port and industry
cons: A city less economically developed than the big centres
Fewer opportunities in IT
Lower prestige than the big universities

uoradea.about: A state university in Oradea, with medicine, science, engineering, law, arts and theology. It is the university centre of the north-west of the country.
uoradea.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
uoradea.admission: The admission method differs from one faculty to another: at most the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, at medicine and pharmacy there is a multiple-choice test, and for arts, architecture and sport there are aptitude tests. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
uoradea.scholarshipsNote: The university gives performance scholarships, for very good academic results, in research or in sport, and social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the scholarship regulations.
uoradea.dormsNote: There are student dormitories; there are few compared with the demand, so apply early.
pros: A beautiful, clean city that is developing
Close to the border with Hungary
A varied offer, from medicine to the arts
cons: Fewer large IT companies than in Cluj
Lower prestige than the big universities
Dormitories with limited places

umfst.about: A university of medicine and science in Târgu Mureș, with programmes in Romanian, Hungarian and English. It is named after George Emil Palade, a Nobel laureate.
umfst.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
umfst.admission: For Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy there is a written multiple-choice test, which counts the most, along with the Baccalaureate (bac) average. For nursing and other health programmes the bac average counts, while for engineering, computer science, letters, economics and law the high-school averages count, with no exam. For sport and architecture there are practical tests. A medical certificate is also required.
umfst.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
umfst.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: Programmes in Romanian, Hungarian and English
University hospitals in the city
Newer fields, such as medical IT and engineering
cons: Competitive admission to medicine
A small city, with a limited cultural life
The schedule is heavy

usv-suceava.about: A state university in Suceava, with faculties of engineering, economics, letters, law and forestry. It is the university centre of northern Moldavia.
usv-suceava.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
usv-suceava.admission: The admission method differs from one faculty to another: at most the Baccalaureate (bac) average and grades count, at the Faculty of Medicine and Biological Sciences there is also a written test (multiple-choice) for some programmes, and for sport a sports test. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
usv-suceava.scholarshipsNote: You can receive scholarships to encourage performance, if you have outstanding academic results, and social scholarships, if your family's situation requires it; there are also special scholarships and scholarships for sporting performance.
usv-suceava.dormsNote: It has student dormitories, but places are limited and are usually given according to grades.
pros: Low living costs
A strong forestry faculty, in an area with forests
Small groups, with attention to students
cons: A small city, with fewer entry-level jobs
Lower prestige than the big universities
Many students leave for other cities after graduating

upg.about: A state university in Ploiești, known for petroleum and gas engineering. It trains engineers for industry and also has faculties of economic sciences and of letters and sciences.
upg.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
upg.admission: You get in with the Baccalaureate (bac) average, with no exam in mathematics or physics. Only a few programmes have a further test: a multiple-choice test for Psychology and eliminatory tests for pedagogy and foreign languages. Check the admission guide.
upg.scholarshipsNote: There are performance scholarships, for outstanding academic results, and social scholarships; in addition there are scholarships offered by companies and foundations, such as the Romgaz Scholarship.
upg.dormsNote: There are student dormitories right next to the university, and the university says it can meet all accommodation requests.
pros: A rare specialisation in oil and gas, in demand in industry
Close to Bucharest, easy to reach
Companies in the field hire graduates
cons: The oil field is declining in favour of green energy
A narrower offer than at a large university
The city does not have an equally active student life

uab.about: A state university in Alba Iulia, with faculties of history, law, theology, economics and computer science. It is a smaller university in a historic city.
uab.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
uab.admission: For almost all programmes only the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts. For a few, an aptitude test is added (for example in sport or pedagogy) or an interview (for example in theology). Read the criteria of the programme you are interested in.
uab.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
uab.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: A historic, quiet and safe city
Small groups, with attention from teachers
Low living costs
cons: A small city, with a modest student life
A narrower offer than the big universities
Fewer local job opportunities

valahia.about: A state university in Târgoviște, with faculties of engineering, economics, law, humanities and theology. It is the university centre of Dâmbovița county.
valahia.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
valahia.admission: At most faculties only the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts. For sport, music and educational sciences you also take aptitude tests, and for theology a written exam. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
valahia.scholarshipsNote: You can receive merit scholarships for good grades, and social scholarships if your family's situation requires it.
valahia.dormsNote: It has student dormitories, but places are limited and are usually given according to grades.
pros: Close to Bucharest, easy to commute
Low living costs in a historic city
Smaller groups, with attention to students
cons: A narrower offer than the big universities
Fewer local job opportunities
Student life is modest

ub-bacau.about: A state university in Bacău, with faculties of engineering, science, letters, economics and physical education. It is the main university centre in southern Moldavia.
ub-bacau.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
ub-bacau.admission: For the bachelor's you do not take a written exam: the Baccalaureate (bac) average and the averages of your high-school years count. For sport you take practical tests, and for pedagogy an eliminatory aptitude test. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
ub-bacau.scholarshipsNote: There are merit and social scholarships, and some students can also receive performance scholarships.
ub-bacau.dormsNote: There are student dormitories; there are few compared with the demand, so apply early.

Low living costs
Partnerships with companies in local industry
cons: The city has fewer IT jobs
Lower prestige than the big universities
Many young people leave for other cities after university

uav-arad.about: A state university in Arad, with faculties of engineering, economics, humanities, physical education, theology and arts. It is near the western border.
uav-arad.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
uav-arad.admission: At most faculties the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, with no written exam. For design and sport you take aptitude tests, for pedagogy an eliminatory test, and for theology an interview. Read the guide of the faculty you are interested in.
uav-arad.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
uav-arad.dormsNote: It offers accommodation in dormitories, depending on your grade average and your situation; other students rent in the city.
pros: Close to Timișoara and the border with Hungary
A quiet city, with moderate costs
A varied offer, including arts and theology
cons: Fewer options than at a large university
Lower prestige than those in the big centres
A more limited student life

utgjiu.about: A state university in Târgu Jiu, Brâncuși's city, with four faculties: engineering, economic sciences, education, law and public administration, and medical sciences and sport. It is the university centre of Gorj.
utgjiu.budgetNote: It has state-funded places with no tuition fee, and the fee-paying ones are cheaper than in Western Europe.
utgjiu.admission: At all faculties the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, along with the grade from the first written test of the bac. For a few programmes, eliminatory pass/fail tests are added: drawing and an interview for Design, sports tests for sport and physiotherapy, a multiple-choice test for nursing and pharmacy assistance, and an aptitude test for pedagogy.
utgjiu.scholarshipsNote: You can receive merit scholarships for good grades, and social scholarships if your family's situation requires it.
utgjiu.dormsNote: It has student dormitories, but places are limited and are usually given according to grades.
pros: Very low living costs
Small groups and approachable teachers
A city with the Brâncuși Ensemble, full of culture
cons: A small city, with few jobs for graduates
A narrower offer
Lower national prestige

upet.about: A state university in Petroșani, known for its mining faculty and for electrical and mechanical engineering. It also has programmes in economics and administration.
upet.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
upet.admission: You do not take an admission exam: an average is calculated between the Baccalaureate (bac) average and the grade from one written bac test (for engineering, mathematics). The test taken into account differs by faculty, so check the admission guide.
upet.scholarshipsNote: There are performance scholarships for good academic results and social scholarships, and good athletes can receive a scholarship for sporting performance.
upet.dormsNote: There are student dormitories; there are few compared with the demand, so apply early.

Small groups, with attention to students

aft-sibiu.about: A state military institution in Sibiu that trains officers for the Land Forces. Students receive military training and specialist studies.
aft-sibiu.budgetNote: You do not pay tuition for the bachelor's: all places are paid for by the state, for the army and for other defence and public order institutions.
aft-sibiu.admission: First you go through recruitment and selection: psychological assessment, physical tests, an interview and a medical examination. Then you take a written test, a multiple-choice test in mathematics, computer science and physics. Start at the information and recruitment office in your county.
aft-sibiu.scholarshipsNote: As a military student you do not pay tuition, and accommodation, meals and equipment are free. For the monthly pay (soldă), ask the information and recruitment office.
aft-sibiu.dormsNote: Accommodation and meals are provided on site, usually for the whole period of study.
pros: A guaranteed post in the army after graduation
Accommodation, food and an allowance provided
Practical training and discipline, useful in life
cons: A strict life, with a military schedule
You are obliged to work in the army for a number of years
The physical and medical tests are eliminatory

afa-brasov.about: A state military institution in Brașov that trains officers for the Air Force and specialists in aviation and air management. It is named after the aviation pioneer Henri Coandă.
afa-brasov.budgetNote: All bachelor's places are funded from the state budget, so you do not pay tuition. No fee is paid for the admission competition either.
afa-brasov.admission: You apply through the army's information and recruitment office. First you pass the eliminatory tests (psychological assessment, sports tests, an interview and a medical examination), then you take a multiple-choice test in mathematics, computer science and physics. You also need an English certificate at B2 level, which can be the one from the Baccalaureate (bac).
afa-brasov.scholarshipsNote: As a military student you do not pay tuition, and accommodation, meals and equipment are free. For the monthly pay (soldă), ask the information and recruitment office.
afa-brasov.dormsNote: Accommodation and meals are provided free of charge during your studies. On the days of the admission competition you arrange your own accommodation and meals.
pros: Training in aviation and air defence
Accommodation, food and an allowance provided
A guaranteed post in the army
cons: A strict life, with military discipline
You are obliged to work in the army for a number of years
Very demanding medical tests are required

unap.about: A state military institution in Bucharest for the training and further training of officers, mainly at master's and doctoral level and through courses. It is aimed mainly at those who are already in the army.
unap.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you get good grades at admission; the other places are fee-paying.
unap.admission: Admission requires written tests, physical tests and a medical check, as at any military institution; strict entry rules apply. Ask the institution for information.
unap.scholarshipsNote: You receive accommodation, food and a monthly allowance during your studies, on top of the usual scholarships.
unap.dormsNote: Accommodation and meals are provided on site, usually for the whole period of study.
pros: Advanced studies in defence and security
Links with military structures in the country and abroad
Courses and master's programmes useful for a military career
cons: It is not an ordinary faculty for high-school graduates

An offer limited to the military field

uat-tgmures.about: A state university in Târgu Mureș, with programmes in acting, directing, puppetry, choreography, set design, music and audiovisual communication. It has one faculty in Romanian and one in Hungarian.
uat-tgmures.budgetNote: State-funded places are tuition-free, and if you do not get one you can choose a fee-paying place, which is more affordable than abroad.
uat-tgmures.admission: For acting and puppetry you take practical talent tests: musical and rhythm aptitudes, poems, a monologue, improvisation. For audiovisual communication you have an introductory interview and the Baccalaureate (bac) average also counts. Details differ by programme.
uat-tgmures.scholarshipsNote: Scholarships are given for grades, along with social scholarships; you can find the conditions in the university's regulations.
uat-tgmures.dormsNote: It has a small dormitory with few rooms, and the places are shared out by a university committee; many students rent in the city.

Its own university theatre for performances

A very narrow field

rau.about: A private university in Bucharest, with faculties of law, management-marketing, managerial informatics and tourism. It was founded in the 1990s and follows the model of American universities.

rau.scholarshipsNote: Some of the students with the highest admission averages receive a place free of charge (a full study scholarship); the conditions are in the scholarship regulations.
rau.dormsNote: It has a dormitory on campus, with rooms for 1–3 people with their own bathroom; places are limited and are paid for separately, so apply early.

utm.about: A private university in Bucharest, known for its faculty of medicine and its faculty of dental medicine, plus law and psychology. It is named after the critic Titu Maiorescu.
utm.budgetNote: It is a private university and you pay a tuition fee: at most programmes it is low, but for medicine, dental medicine and pharmacy it is much higher.
utm.admission: For Medicine you take an exam: a multiple-choice test in biology and, as you choose, in chemistry or physics. For Nursing a biology test and the Baccalaureate (bac) average count. At the other faculties the rules are different, so read the methodology of your faculty.
utm.scholarshipsNote: You can ask the secretariat whether there are scholarships or fee reductions for good results.
utm.dormsNote: It has two student dormitories in Bucharest; you submit an application, and places are shared out according to the dormitory regulations.

Partner hospitals for practical training

For Medicine you take an admission exam, as at the state universities

univnt.about: A private university in Bucharest, specialising in law and in economic and administrative sciences. It is named after the diplomat Nicolae Titulescu.
univnt.budgetNote: It has no state-funded places, but the fees are generally affordable and you can pay them in instalments.
univnt.admission: At all faculties, admission to the bachelor's is based on the Baccalaureate (bac) average, with no exam and no interview: you submit your file and are ranked by average.
univnt.scholarshipsNote: Students with very good results can receive merit scholarships and special scholarships; there are also fee reductions, for example for siblings or spouses who study here.
univnt.dormsNote: It has its own dormitory in Bucharest, with rooms for 2–4 people with their own bathroom; you get a place as far as places are available, so ask early.

ucdc.about: A private university with faculties in Bucharest and Cluj-Napoca, for law, administration, economics, foreign languages and education. It is named after the scholar Dimitrie Cantemir.
ucdc.budgetNote: It is a private university, so you pay a fee; it is generally lower than at private universities in Western Europe.

ucdc.scholarshipsNote: There are fee reductions, for example for the students with the highest averages each year and for those who pay the whole fee at once; ask the secretariat about scholarships.

spiru-haret.about: A private university that presents itself as the largest in Romania, with faculties in Bucharest, Brașov, Craiova, Constanța and Câmpulung and with many fields. It is named after the mathematician and school reformer Spiru Haret.
spiru-haret.budgetNote: It has no state-funded places, but the fees are generally affordable and you can pay them in instalments.

spiru-haret.scholarshipsNote: The university has a scholarship regulation and offers a few full study scholarships for high-school students (the “Liceenii” Scholarship); ask the secretariat what the conditions are.
spiru-haret.dormsNote: Do not count on a dormitory: ask at admission or look for a rental in the city.

Simple admission and affordable fees

Not all programmes have the same reputation with employers
Check that the programme you choose is accredited

sapientia.about: A private university teaching in Hungarian. The rectorate is in Cluj-Napoca, and the faculties are in four cities: Miercurea Ciuc, Târgu Mureș, Cluj-Napoca and Sfântu Gheorghe. It is aimed especially at young Hungarians in Romania.

sapientia.scholarshipsNote: The university gives merit scholarships, study scholarships and social scholarships, according to its own regulations.
sapientia.dormsNote: It has dormitories or accommodation for students; places are limited, so ask early.

Technical and applied science programmes
