uvvg.about: A private university in Arad, known for its faculties of medicine, dental medicine and pharmacy. It also has law, economics and computer science.
uvvg.budgetNote: It is a private university: at most programmes the fee is low, but for medicine it is much higher; ask which instalments are possible.
uvvg.admission: For medicine, dental medicine and pharmacy you take a written multiple-choice test (biology and chemistry; for pharmacy, biology). For the other programmes, for example nursing, dental technology or nutrition, the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts. The rules differ by faculty.
uvvg.scholarshipsNote: The university announces excellence, merit and social scholarships; ask the secretariat what conditions you must meet.
uvvg.dormsNote: It has its own dormitory in Arad, close to the campus, with a canteen in the same building; places are limited, so ask early.
pros: You can study medicine in a smaller city, without the competition for state-funded places
Partner clinics and hospitals in the area
Close to Timișoara and the border with Hungary
cons: Fees for medicine are much higher
Lower prestige than the state medical universities
A small city, with a limited cultural offer

upa-iasi.about: A private university in Iași, founded in 1990, which presents itself as the largest private higher education institution in Moldavia. It has two faculties: one of law, economics, political and administrative sciences, and one of psychology, educational sciences and social work.
upa-iasi.budgetNote: It is a private university, so you pay a fee; it is generally lower than at private universities in Western Europe.
upa-iasi.admission: You do not take an exam: you submit your file (also online), and the admission average is calculated from the Baccalaureate (bac) average and the grade from the written Romanian language test of the bac.
upa-iasi.scholarshipsNote: The university has a regulation for awarding scholarships; ask the secretariat what conditions you must meet.
upa-iasi.dormsNote: Do not count on a dormitory: ask at admission or look for a rental in the city.
pros: Programmes in social sciences and law
Accessible admission, based on your file
Small groups, with more attention
cons: You pay a tuition fee
Lower prestige than UAIC
A limited offer, only two faculties

hyperion.about: A private university in Bucharest, founded in 1990, with seven faculties: law, economics, journalism, psychology, exact and engineering sciences, social sciences and humanities, arts.
hyperion.budgetNote: It has no state-funded places, but the fees are generally affordable and you can pay them in instalments.
hyperion.admission: At most programmes you get in on the basis of your file, with your Baccalaureate (bac) diploma and average. At the Faculty of Psychology and Educational Sciences and the Faculty of Arts, admission is by exam. Read the methodology on the website.
hyperion.scholarshipsNote: The website announces fee reductions and scholarships for students with very high averages, at some programmes, and a reduction when two members of the same family enrol.
hyperion.dormsNote: The university has its own student hostel in Bucharest, with rooms with a bathroom; places are reserved in advance, by phone.
pros: A varied offer for a private university
A faculty of journalism and of arts in the capital
Small groups and approachable teachers
cons: You pay a tuition fee
Less well known than the state universities
Practical training depends a lot on the faculty

ueb.about: A private university in Bucharest, with six faculties: law, psychology, financial management, communication sciences, ecology and environmental protection, physical education and sport. It puts the emphasis on the environment and sustainable development.
ueb.budgetNote: It is a private university, so you pay a fee; it is generally lower than at private universities in Western Europe.
ueb.admission: Admission is a competition of files: the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts, with no exam. For Physical Education and Sport there is also a practical test. The rules may differ by faculty.
ueb.scholarshipsNote: The university gives performance scholarships, according to its own regulations, and a small reduction if you pay the whole fee at the start.
ueb.dormsNote: Do not count on a dormitory: ask at admission or look for a rental in the city.
pros: Specialisation in the environment and ecological management
Accessible admission, based on your file
A schedule that also suits those who work
cons: You pay a tuition fee
Less well known than the state universities
Fewer programmes than at the large universities

danubius.about: A private university in Galați (until 2024 it was called the “Danubius” University of Galați), with five faculties: law and international governance, business and leadership, media, design and technology, life sciences and human development, and education. It is in the south-east of Moldavia.
danubius.budgetNote: It is a private university, so you pay a tuition fee. You can pay it all at once or in instalments.
danubius.admission: You take no exam and have no interview: only the overall Baccalaureate (bac) average counts. The exception is Primary Education Pedagogy, which also has two eliminatory aptitude tests. There is also a pre-admission for pupils, based on high-school averages. You can apply online.
danubius.scholarshipsNote: The university gives scholarships and prizes for outstanding merit and fee reductions for involvement in activities.
danubius.dormsNote: Do not count on a dormitory: ask at admission or look for a rental in the city.
pros: Offers modern programmes: media, design and technology
Accessible admission, based on your file
Small groups, with attention to students
cons: You pay a tuition fee
Less well known than the state universities
A city with fewer opportunities than the big centres

ucb-pitesti.about: A private university based in Pitești, with faculties in three cities: Pitești, Râmnicu Vâlcea and Brăila. You can study management, accounting, trade and tourism, law and public administration; most programmes are in Râmnicu Vâlcea.
ucb-pitesti.budgetNote: It is a private university, so you usually pay a fee. There are, however, a few places with no fee, paid for by the university, for those who win the pre-admission competition. Ask the secretariat about instalments.
ucb-pitesti.admission: Admission is based on your file and the Baccalaureate (bac) average. Check the rules for each faculty on the website.
ucb-pitesti.scholarshipsNote: The university offers, from its own funds, places with no fee, which are won in a pre-admission competition with a multiple-choice test, plus merit scholarships and social assistance scholarships.
ucb-pitesti.dormsNote: Do not count on a dormitory; ask at admission or look for a rental in the city.
pros: You can study economics or law in Pitești without moving
It also has faculties in Râmnicu Vâlcea and Brăila
Simple admission, based on your file
cons: You pay a tuition fee
The range of fields is narrower than at the large universities
Fewer student activities than in a big centre

andrei-saguna.about: A private, non-profit university in Constanța, with bachelor's programmes in law, psychology, management, accounting and public administration. It has been accredited by law since 2005.
andrei-saguna.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable; there are no state-funded places.
andrei-saguna.admission: You get in on the basis of the Baccalaureate (bac) average, with no extra exams. For some programmes you also have a motivation talk of a few minutes with a teacher, who cannot eliminate you. You can apply online.
andrei-saguna.scholarshipsNote: Ask the secretariat whether there are scholarships or fee reductions for good results.
andrei-saguna.dormsNote: The university has its own accommodation in Constanța, which students can also use, with the approval of the management. Ask early whether there are places.
pros: You can study by the sea, in a city with many activities in summer
Law and psychology programmes in a small university
Admission without a hard exam
cons: You pay a tuition fee
A small university, less well known outside the region
The range of programmes is narrower

george-bacovia.about: A private university in Bacău, accredited by ARACIS, with a single faculty, of economic, legal and administrative sciences. You can study management, trade and tourism, law, public administration and computer science.
george-bacovia.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable; there are no state-funded places.
george-bacovia.admission: Admission is based on your file, with no exam and no interview: candidates are ranked by their Baccalaureate (bac) average. You can also apply online. Read the admission regulations on the website.
george-bacovia.scholarshipsNote: The university gives merit scholarships in the form of a fee reduction for very good results; the graduates' association and the Bacovia Foundation also contribute to the scholarship fund.
george-bacovia.dormsNote: Check with the secretariat whether the university offers accommodation for students; otherwise, look early for a rental in Bacău.
pros: Scholarships also offered by graduates and a foundation
You study economics or law in a smaller, quiet city
Courses supported by an online platform
cons: You pay a tuition fee
A single faculty, so few fields
Less well known outside the region

emanuel-oradea.about: A private Christian Baptist university in Oradea, with theology and management, plus programmes such as music, social work and English language. It teaches in Romanian.
emanuel-oradea.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable; there are no state-funded places.
emanuel-oradea.admission: For all programmes you have a motivation interview and a test on the Baptist Confession of Faith. For management and economic informatics you also take a test, for music an aptitude test, and for Romanian-English an English interview. As a rule you must be a baptised member of an evangelical church and bring a recommendation from the pastor.
emanuel-oradea.scholarshipsNote: The university has a scholarship for results and involvement (“Integrity and Excellence”) and a tuition scholarship; the conditions are in the scholarship regulations.
emanuel-oradea.dormsNote: It has accommodation and meals on campus, plus a chapel and a medical office.
pros: A campus with accommodation, a canteen and services for students
Baptist theology, a rare programme in the country
A small community, where the teachers know you
cons: You pay a tuition fee
A confessional environment: as a rule, baptised members of evangelical churches are accepted
Few fields apart from theology and management

partium.about: A private university in Oradea, the first accredited private university in Romania teaching in Hungarian. It has two faculties: one of letters and arts and one of economic and social sciences, teaching mainly in Hungarian.
partium.budgetNote: Although it is a private university, some of the places have no fee and the rest are fee-paying. Each year the places are reallocated according to academic results.
partium.admission: Admission is generally based on your file, with the Baccalaureate (bac) average; for some programmes there may also be a test. The programmes are taught mostly in Hungarian, so you need to know it well.
partium.scholarshipsNote: The university gives merit scholarships, study scholarships and social scholarships, plus an excellence scholarship for students on the economics programmes.
partium.dormsNote: It has its own dormitory in Oradea, with rooms for 2–4 people and a canteen in the building; ask early how places are given.
pros: You can study in Hungarian in Romania
A small university, with attention to students
Programmes in letters, economics and arts in one place
cons: No-fee places are limited; for the others you pay a fee
You need Hungarian for most programmes
The range of programmes is limited

agora-oradea.about: A private university in Oradea, with a faculty of economic sciences and a faculty of legal and administrative sciences. It offers bachelor's and master's studies.
agora-oradea.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable; there are no state-funded places.
agora-oradea.admission: You get in without an exam, on the basis of your file: your place in the ranking depends on your Baccalaureate (bac) average. You can also apply online. For details, see the admission page.
agora-oradea.scholarshipsNote: It has three kinds of scholarships that cover the fee, in full or in part: the Agora Scholarship, won through a competition at admission, the merit scholarship and the social scholarship.
agora-oradea.dormsNote: Do not count on a dormitory; ask at admission or look for a rental in the city.
pros: You can study law or economics in Oradea
Courses supported by an online platform
Simple admission, without an exam
cons: You pay a tuition fee
Only two faculties
Less well known than the state universities in the city

tibiscus.about: A private university in Timișoara, with four faculties: computers and applied informatics, law and public administration, psychology, and economic sciences.
tibiscus.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable; there are no state-funded places.
tibiscus.admission: Admission is through a competition of files, with no exam. For law, for example, the admission average is calculated from the Baccalaureate (bac) average and the Romanian language averages from high school. Each faculty has its own methodology, so read it on the website.
tibiscus.scholarshipsNote: The university offers reductions on the tuition fee, called social scholarships and merit scholarships (for very good academic or research results). You receive them on the basis of an application submitted to the faculty secretariat.
tibiscus.dormsNote: Do not count on a dormitory; ask at admission or look for a rental in the city.
pros: You can study computer science or psychology in Timișoara
A large student city, with many opportunities
Smaller groups than at the state universities
cons: You pay a tuition fee
Only four faculties, with few programmes
Less well known than the big state universities in the city

apollonia.about: A private university in Iași, with two faculties. The Faculty of Medicine has programmes such as dental medicine, dental technology, general nursing and balneophysiokinetotherapy, and at the Faculty of Communication Sciences you can study communication and journalism.
apollonia.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable; there are no state-funded places. Medical studies usually have higher fees than economics ones.
apollonia.admission: At the Faculty of Medicine (dental medicine, dental technology, nursing and others) you take a multiple-choice test and an interview in biology (human anatomy and physiology), which counts the most; the rest of the average comes from the Baccalaureate (bac) average. For communication, an interview and the bac average count.
apollonia.scholarshipsNote: Ask the secretariat whether there are scholarships or fee reductions for good results.
apollonia.dormsNote: Do not count on a dormitory; ask at admission or look for a rental in the city.
pros: Focused on dental medicine and related fields
Iași is a large university centre
Training in an environment specialised in dentistry
cons: You pay a tuition fee, higher for medicine
A narrow offer: only health and communication
Medical studies demand a lot of work and money for materials

athenaeum.about: A private university in Bucharest, with a faculty of economic sciences and a faculty of public administration. The bachelor's programmes generally last three years.
athenaeum.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable; there are no state-funded places.
athenaeum.admission: Admission is generally based on your file, with the Baccalaureate (bac) average. For the exact rules, see the admission page.
athenaeum.scholarshipsNote: Ask the secretariat whether there are scholarships or fee reductions for good results.
athenaeum.dormsNote: The university has no dormitory of its own, but has an agreement with a few dormitories; the accommodation request is submitted to the secretariat at the start of the academic year.
pros: You can study economic informatics or management in the capital
Three-year programmes, shorter
Simple admission, based on your file
cons: You pay a tuition fee
Only two faculties
Less well known than the large state universities

bioterra.about: A private university in Bucharest, accredited by law in 2002. It has programmes in agriculture and rural development, law, food products and nursing, in Bucharest and in Buzău.
bioterra.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable; there are no state-funded places.
bioterra.admission: Admission is generally based on your file and the Baccalaureate (bac) average. The methodology is published on the website every year.
bioterra.scholarshipsNote: The website says there are merit scholarships and social scholarships, in the form of a partial or total fee waiver, and a reduction when several family members study here; ask the secretariat about the conditions.
bioterra.dormsNote: The website presents a university complex with five student dormitories and a canteen-restaurant; ask at admission how to get a place.
pros: Rare programmes at a private university: agriculture and food products
Accessible admission, without a hard exam
It also has a branch in another city, Buzău
cons: You pay a tuition fee
Less well known than the state universities
The faculties are small, with fewer activities

artifex.about: A private university in Bucharest, with a faculty of finance and accounting and a faculty of management and marketing. Its bachelor's programmes are accredited.
artifex.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable; there are no state-funded places.
artifex.admission: You get in on the basis of your file: the admission average is the average of the Baccalaureate (bac) grade and the average of your high-school years. See the rules and open programmes on the website.
artifex.scholarshipsNote: Ask the secretariat whether there are scholarships or fee reductions for good results.
artifex.dormsNote: The university has its own dormitory in Bucharest, in Sector 6, with rooms for one, two or three people; accommodation is paid for.
pros: You can study finance, management or marketing in the capital
A small university, with small groups
The bachelor's programmes are accredited
cons: You pay a tuition fee
The offer is limited to economics
Less well known than the large universities of economics

adventus.about: A private Adventist university near Bucharest, with the Faculty of Theology and Social Sciences. It has bachelor's degrees in pastoral Adventist theology, social work, primary education pedagogy and early education, all in Romanian.
adventus.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable; there are no state-funded places.
adventus.admission: For all programmes there is first an eliminatory interview. For Theology you then take tests in biblical knowledge, Romanian and English, and you must be a baptised member of the Adventist Church; for Social Work and Pedagogy the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts.
adventus.scholarshipsNote: The university gives study, merit and social scholarships; Theology students supported by the Conference they belong to do not pay the tuition fee.
adventus.dormsNote: It has student dormitories and a canteen on campus; accommodation and meals are paid for.
pros: A small, close-knit community in a quiet place
The theology programme has been re-accredited by ARACIS
Very small groups, with attention to each student
cons: You pay a tuition fee
It suits mainly those from the Adventist community
Only four bachelor's programmes

ani-bucuresti.about: A state institution in Bucharest that belongs to the Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) and trains intelligence officers. The bachelor's lasts three years and has two tracks: operations officer and analyst officer.
ani-bucuresti.budgetNote: The places are state-funded, so you do not pay tuition; if you drop out along the way, the study contract provides that you repay the maintenance and training costs.
ani-bucuresti.admission: First you go through a selection made by the SRI: interviews, tests, a psychological examination, a medical examination and security checks. Only then do you take the academy's competition, with a general knowledge test and an aptitude test; the Baccalaureate (bac) and high-school averages count a little. You apply from winter and there is an age limit.
ani-bucuresti.scholarshipsNote: The student guide says that the institution provides accommodation, meals and equipment for all military students.
ani-bucuresti.dormsNote: The academy has accommodation on campus for students. Check the academy's website whether you also receive accommodation on the days of the admission competition.
pros: You pay no fee, and accommodation and meals are provided
After graduation you are assigned to an SRI unit
Training that is rare in the country: intelligence analysis and operations
cons: A long selection, with medical, psychological and security checks
You are a military student, with strict rules and many restrictions
You must accept to work anywhere in the country

itb-bucuresti.about: A confessional school at university level, under the spiritual authority of the Baptist Union of Romania, which trains ministers for Baptist churches. It has a single bachelor's degree, pastoral Baptist theology, full-time and distance learning.
itb-bucuresti.budgetNote: It has no state-funded places, but the annual fee is small and can be paid in instalments; the website says the institute covers most of the real cost of tuition.
itb-bucuresti.admission: First there is an eliminatory oral test: an interview and questions from the Baptist Confession of Faith. Then an essay sent with your file is graded, and the Baccalaureate (bac) average counts too; you need recommendations from your church.
itb-bucuresti.scholarshipsNote: All students receive financial support for the fee, accommodation and canteen; in addition there is a merit scholarship and a few social scholarships.
itb-bucuresti.dormsNote: It has a dormitory and canteen at the headquarters on Str. Berzei, for pastoral theology students, and another, larger dormitory in the city.
pros: Low costs, with support for the fee, accommodation and meals
Dormitory and canteen right at the headquarters
You can also study by distance learning
cons: It suits only those who want to serve in Baptist churches
You need recommendations from the pastor and the church
A single programme and very few full-time places

itp-bucuresti.about: A private theological institute in Bucharest, accredited by law in 2008, which trains ministers for Pentecostal churches. The bachelor's in pastoral Pentecostal theology lasts four years.
itp-bucuresti.budgetNote: It has no state-funded places; the annual fee is small compared with other private faculties, and accommodation and meals are paid separately.
itp-bucuresti.admission: There are two tests: an interview with public speaking, which is eliminatory, and a written test of biblical knowledge. You must be a baptised member of a Pentecostal church and have recommendations from your church.
itp-bucuresti.scholarshipsNote: The candidate with the highest grade on the written test receives a scholarship; siblings who study at the same time pay a reduced fee and there is support for accommodation and meals, within the limits of funds.
itp-bucuresti.dormsNote: It has a dormitory with rooms for three to four people, with their own bathroom, and a canteen on course days; both are paid for.
pros: Dormitory and canteen at the institute
A small fee and reductions for siblings
A small group, in a close-knit community
cons: It is only for baptised members of Pentecostal churches
A single bachelor's programme
The degree prepares you mainly for service in the church

bogdan-voda.about: A private university in Cluj-Napoca, with over 30 years of activity and three faculties: Law, Economic Sciences and Physical Education and Sport.
bogdan-voda.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable; there are no state-funded places.
bogdan-voda.admission: For Law and Economic Sciences the Baccalaureate (bac) average and the average of your high-school years count. For Physical Education and Sport you also take an eliminatory practical sports test: sprint, standing long jump and push-ups.
bogdan-voda.scholarshipsNote: The university has a scholarship regulation and other forms of support for students; ask the secretariat what conditions you must meet.
bogdan-voda.dormsNote: We found no information about a dormitory on the website; ask at admission or look for a rental in the city.
pros: Admission without a written exam for Law and Economic Sciences
You can study sport in a big student city
It also has part-time courses
cons: You pay a tuition fee
Only three faculties, with few programmes
Less well known than the state universities in Cluj

itp-cluj.about: A theological institute in the centre of Cluj that trains pastors for the Reformed, Evangelical-Lutheran and Unitarian churches in Transylvania. The bachelor's in pastoral Protestant theology lasts four years and is taught in Hungarian.
itp-cluj.budgetNote: The admission pages mention an enrolment fee and the cost of the boarding house and meals, announced before enrolment; ask the secretariat what you pay per year.
itp-cluj.admission: For the Reformed track you first take part in a pre-admission camp with an interview, then take oral tests on the Bible and the catechism, a church singing test and Hungarian. You must be a member of the church and have your community's recommendation; each church has its own rules.
itp-cluj.scholarshipsNote: There are study, merit, performance and social scholarships, offered by churches and partner foundations in Hungary, the Netherlands and other countries.
itp-cluj.dormsNote: The institute has a boarding house in its own building for Reformed and Lutheran students; Unitarian students live in a separate dormitory.
pros: A boarding house right in the institute's building, in the centre of Cluj
Many kinds of scholarships, plus study scholarships in Western Europe
Three Protestant traditions in the same school
cons: Teaching and admission are in Hungarian
It is only for members of the churches that support the institute
A single programme, which prepares you to be a pastor

dragan-lugoj.about: A private university in Lugoj, Timiș county, which started classes in the 1992/1993 academic year. It has two faculties: Law and Economic Sciences.
dragan-lugoj.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable, in instalments; there are no state-funded places.
dragan-lugoj.admission: You do not take an exam: you submit your file, and the admission average is your Baccalaureate (bac) average. Candidates are admitted in order of averages, as places allow.
dragan-lugoj.scholarshipsNote: The admission regulations provide fee reductions, for example for pupils with prizes at olympiads and competitions, and exemptions from the enrolment fee for some categories.
dragan-lugoj.dormsNote: We found no information about a dormitory on the website; ask at admission or look for a rental in the city.
pros: Simple admission, based on the Baccalaureate (bac) average
Fee reductions for results at olympiads and competitions
A small, quiet town, close to Timișoara
cons: You pay a tuition fee
Only two bachelor's programmes
A small town, with fewer places for practical training and work

cantemir-tgmures.about: A private university in Târgu Mureș, with faculties of dental medicine, law, economic sciences, geography and psychology. It has its own student dormitory.
cantemir-tgmures.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable, in instalments; there are no state-funded places, and dental medicine costs much more than the other programmes.
cantemir-tgmures.admission: For Law, Psychology, Tourism Geography and Economics of Trade, Tourism and Services you get in on the basis of the Baccalaureate (bac) average. For Dental Medicine you take a multiple-choice test, based on a bibliography published by the faculty.
cantemir-tgmures.scholarshipsNote: We found no scholarships or reductions on the admission and fees pages; ask the secretariat.
cantemir-tgmures.dormsNote: It has its own dormitory in Târgu Mureș, with three-bed rooms and a bathroom in the room; you submit your request at the admission centre.
pros: Its own dormitory, with a bathroom in every room
You can study dental medicine at a private university
Admission based on the Baccalaureate (bac) average for most programmes
cons: You pay a tuition fee, high for dental medicine
Only one bachelor's programme per faculty
Less well known than the state university in the city

timotheus.about: A theological institute at university level in Bucharest, founded in 1992 by the Christian Church According to the Gospel of Romania. It has a four-year bachelor's in pastoral theology.
timotheus.budgetNote: It is a private school, with no state-funded places; the website only mentions the enrolment fee, so ask the secretariat what you pay per year.
timotheus.admission: You apply online, then have an eliminatory interview, also online. You also write an essay on a given topic, and the average takes into account the essay grade and the Baccalaureate (bac) average; members of the church need a recommendation.
timotheus.scholarshipsNote: The website says the institute gives merit scholarships and study scholarships; details are requested from the secretariat.
timotheus.dormsNote: We found no information about accommodation on the website; ask the secretariat before you apply.
pros: Online enrolment and interview
There are merit and study scholarships
A small group, with attention to each student
cons: It suits mainly those from the Christian Church According to the Gospel
A single bachelor's programme
We found no information about accommodation on the website

ioan-slavici.about: A private university in Timișoara, founded in 2000 within the foundation of the same name. It has a faculty of engineering, with information technology, and one of economic sciences.
ioan-slavici.budgetNote: Tuition fees are payable, in instalments; there are no state-funded places, and in engineering the fee is somewhat higher than in economics.
ioan-slavici.admission: You do not take a written exam: you enrol and take a pass/fail interview, and the committee makes the ranking taking the Baccalaureate (bac) average into account. There are two sessions, in summer and in autumn.
ioan-slavici.scholarshipsNote: Students with good results can receive fee reductions, partial or total, and annual prizes.
ioan-slavici.dormsNote: The university has hotel-type dormitories, with priority for its own students, and a canteen-restaurant.
pros: Its own dormitories and canteen
You can study information technology at a private university
Fee reductions for good results
cons: You pay a tuition fee
Only three bachelor's programmes
Less well known than the state universities in Timișoara

upb-pitesti.about: The former University of Pitești, which has been part of POLITEHNICA Bucharest since 2023. It has six faculties in Pitești, from automotive engineering and computers to sciences, economics, law, languages and the arts, and primary-school teaching can also be studied in Alexandria, Câmpulung, Râmnicu Vâlcea and Slatina.
upb-pitesti.budgetNote: You can study for free on a state-funded place if you rank high enough; on fee-paying places you pay a yearly fee, and for some programmes the fee is higher, for example engineering, law, physiotherapy, music, acting and general nursing.
upb-pitesti.admission: For most programmes you are admitted on your school record: your high-school grades in the chosen subjects, your overall averages in years 9 to 11 and your high-school activities count. Sport, music and acting have aptitude tests, general nursing has a written biology test and sacred art has a drawing test; you apply online at admitere.pub.ro.
upb-pitesti.scholarshipsNote: There are merit scholarships, based on grades, and social scholarships for students from low-income families or in special situations; only students on state-funded places can get them.
upb-pitesti.dormsNote: There are halls of residence in Pitești: the cheaper places go to students on state-funded places, while fee-paying students can get places at the full price. You apply at the start of the year, and there is also a canteen with reduced prices for students.
pros: A very wide choice, from automotive engineering and computers to law, psychology, music and theatre
A degree from POLITEHNICA Bucharest, a large university
Primary-school teaching can also be studied in four nearby towns
cons: Fewer engineering programmes than in Bucharest
Fees are higher for some programmes, for example engineering, law, acting and general nursing
Scholarships go only to students on state-funded places
